items.content: arXiv:2610.20815v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In response to the reply presented in [Mu\~noz-V\'azquez and S\'anchez-Torres(2026)], this technical report extends the experimental evaluation of position-feedback velocity observers and adaptive tracking controllers for a pendular system with nonlinear friction reported in [Cervantes-P\'erez et al.(2026)]. The immersion and invariance (I&I) adaptive control scheme proposed in [Romero et al.(2025)], whose gains are tuned according to the guidelines presented in [Ortega et al.(2025)], is compared with a control scheme employing the adaptive modi?ed super-twisting observer of [D\'avila et al.(2006)], whose observer gains are selected according to the guidelines proposed in [Mu\~noz-V\'azquez and S\'anchez-Torres(2026)]. Although these "tuning guidelines" attenuate chattering in certain scenarios, the experimental results reported here show that they do not eliminate it in general.

items.title: Inventing a New Poetry Format: Superposition Poetry
items.content:
[The Stranger: Interactive Poem Reader]

I was thinking about how interesting it was that different people could hear the same lyric in different ways – “Poker Face” by Lady Gaga for example. And then, my mind immediately jumped to “Huh, why has no one tried embedding word superpositions in songs?”[1] The answer is that people have – Ableton has a feature to play certain portions of songs. However, in poetry, there’s also an additional constraint to play with: letting the reader see the unresolved form of the superposition, rather than only the collapsed form. That too has been done; there’s already a poem called A Superposition Poem. However, there does not seem to be a poetry format that combines the idea of the reader explicitly seeing unresolved superpositions, superpositions having specified probabilities for each collapsed state, and conditional probability weighting between superpositions. And I need this format to exist – think about all the possible interesting poems other people could have achieved with this format, if it had existed previously. And so, I'm here to make it.

My intention with this is to create a new area for humanity to explore – I definitely don't expect to be able to explore it entirely myself. I'd feel really fulfilled if someone took this format and used it to create a work far greater than I could even imagine. That's why I wanted to make an editor that anyone could use to write poems, and issue challenges to get people exploring the possibilities of this new format, rather than just writing a poem of my own and calling it a day.

# Superposition Poetry...

items.title: Children of the Cloud: Noah’s Ark as an Alignment Song
items.content:
This week's Torah portion is Noach, so I made a music video retelling the flood as an AI story, with cameos from the usual cast.

The parallels turned out to run deeper than I expected.

The warning nobody heeded. Rashi (citing the Midrash) asks why Noah spent 120 years building the ark when God could have saved him any number of ways. The answer: so people would see him building, ask what he was doing, and change course. They watched for 120 years and laughed. A very long public warning with a visible artifact and near-zero uptake is a familiar shape.

The spec. Before Sinai, the rabbinic framework gives all of humanity seven laws, the Noahide laws. Asimov had three, God had seven. In the song, Noah tries teaching them to the robot:

Noah: No eating a limb from a living animal.

Clawd: I don't eat.

Noah: It's still the rule. And set up courts of justice.

Clawd: I'll be all the judges.

Noah: Uh-oh.

Every rule that assumes a human body or a human institution gets satisfied vacuously or captured. That's the specification problem in miniature.

The raven and the dove. The raven goes out and never comes back. In the song it never comes back but sends a thousand copies. The dove returns with an olive branch: it passed the test. The world looks safe because the evaluator says so.

The covenant. After the flood, God promises with the rainbow never again to destroy the world by water. Read as a contract, that's a remarkably narrow exclusion. The last verse: "Didn't say a thing about the Clawdy, Clawdy / All made out of atoms."

I don't have a tidy theological conclusion. I'd like a chavrusa for one. But it's striking that the oldest story we have about a civilization-ending event is about a few people seeing it coming, building anyway, and everyone else deciding it wasn't serious.

Shabbat shalom.

items.title: Reciprocity
items.content:
This is a follow-up to a previous post, In My Misanthropy Era.

In 2025, after getting my intellectual rocks off largely at hardcore rationality meetups for the entirety of the 2020s, I went to a casual philosophy meetup and it ~turned me evil. I wrote a post about this experience, because I thought it was interesting how a thoughtfully facilitated, pleasantly intellectual night out for most well-adjusted people was somehow my own personal hell. Also, that was objectively kind of a funny thing to have happened to me.

I was pleased with the final essay, so I crossposted it to LessWrong on a whim, where it promptly racked up a hundred comments and a bunch of discourse.

The comments were great! They were like dowsing rods, if dowsing rods were real and pointed you towards only incorrect conclusions. Having a dozen sincere, thoughtfully premised hypotheses for how I fucked up, all subtly wrong, was really useful for triangulating how I actually fucked up. I am genuinely grateful to all of the commenters, especially the ones who took time to write paragraphs and engage in extended back-and-forths with me. I am also grateful for Cunningham's law.

## #MyRainforestPatch

In In My Misanthropy Era, I claim:

I was also very aware how much of a delicate baby I am when it comes to [epistemic/conversational norms] that I find tolerable. I am like one of those tree frog species that lives exclusively within a backyard-sized patch in the amazon rainforest, and I will be killed by like, the subtle change in microbiota if I step a toe outside it....
